headline: Council approves Soleil TIF agreement, $200,000 police overtime funding, but rejects mobile home rent moratorium
summary: The Council held public hearings and took action on several items including a solid waste ordinance amendment, a mobile home park rent moratorium, a credit enhancement agreement for the Soleil housing project, and supplemental police overtime funding. The Council also approved parking changes, forfeiture funds transfer, a property disposition, and a housing authority appointment, while postponing ethics policy amendments and a railroad dissolution order.
decisions: Entered Executive Session to discuss acquisition or disposition of Real Estate.
Approved amendment to Traffic Schedule adding 15-minute parking spots on Pine Street from Horton Street to Prince Street Alley.
Approved acceptance of transfer of forfeiture funds from sale of a 9mm Taurus Pistol to the Drug Enforcement Program account.
Approved disposition of 35 Beechwood Avenue to Ashley Woodbury for $1,000.
Confirmed appointment of Craig Tribuno to the Lewiston Housing Authority Board of Commissioners.
Gave final passage to amendments defining the automated side load trash collection program in the Solid Waste Ordinance.
Motion for first passage of the Moratorium Ordinance on rent increases for mobile home park lots did not pass.
Approved Order authorizing City Administrator to execute a Credit Enhancement Agreement for the Soleil Multi-Family Housing Project.
Motion to amend the Resolve to add $55,000 for a self-deploying drone did not pass.
Approved Resolve authorizing a $200,000 supplemental appropriation from the Salary Reserve account for police overtime.
Postponed amendments to the City's Ethics Policy, Policy Manual Number 94, to the next Council meeting.
Postponed the Order directing the City Administrator to explore dissolution of the Lewiston Auburn Railroad Company to the next Council meeting.
Approved Order directing the City Administrator to request an additional Agency Liquor Store License from the Maine Bureau of Alcoholic Beverages and Lottery Operations.
Entered Executive Session to discuss labor negotiations with MSEA Local 1989 and a personnel matter.

CITY OF LEWISTON 
 
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 4, 2026 
 
REGULAR MEETING HELD IN THE COUNCIL ROOM AT 6:00 P.M. 
 
THE HONORABLE CARL L. SHELINE, MAYOR, PRESIDING. 
          
PRESENT: Mayor Sheline, Councilors Nagine, Longchamps, Harriman, Roy, Chittim, and 
Martel, City Administrator Bryan Kaenrath, Deputy City Administrator Brian O’Malley, and 
City Clerk Kathleen Montejo. Absent/Excused: Councilor Noble.  (Note – Per the City Charter, 
the Mayor may cast a vote in the absence of a City Councilor.) 
 
EXECUTIVE SESSION 
 
VOTE (283-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To enter into an Executive Session, pursuant to MRSA Title 1, section 405(6) (c), to discuss the 
acquisition or disposition of Real Estate, of which the premature disclosure of the information 
would prejudice the competitive bargaining position of the City.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
Executive Session began at 6:03pm and ended at 6:52 pm. 
 
Councilor Noble retired from the meeting at this time.  
 
Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag. 
 
VOTE (284-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
  
To dispense with the reading of the minutes of the meeting of July 21, 2026, and to accept and 
place them on file as prepared by the City Clerk.   Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
Ronnie Paradis, Ward 6 – Thank you to the Council for the last meeting, one of the best in recent 
memory and past meetings.  Thank you to Councilor Longchamps for ongoing public safety 
effort. Talk about issues and not people. Spoke with School Superintendent and discussed a lot 
of ideas about what parents can do for students.  When on School Committee, was a volunteer 
reader at Longley Elementary School, the Councilors should consider doing this activity and get 
to meet kids directly.  
 
Larry Gilbert, Lewiston – Many residents have expressed concerns with Flock cameras, but he 
supports the cameras because of the gun violence. It is a worthy tool for the police department to 
solve crime. When people are in public, there is no expectation of privacy. He became involved 
in law enforcement to help people. More communication between the police and residents is 
needed.
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 4, 2026 
                             
2 
 
Rick LaChapelle, Ward 4 – The city is looking for leadership, particularly about the increase in 
youth gun violence. The Council meeting at the high school was a joke, just a handful of special 
groups saying they need money. The state has funds that should be put aside for youth sports. 
The money spent in the abuse of Medicaid fraud could have benefited the District Attorney’s 
offices to support their work against gun violence. Our state legislators should be advocating for 
more funds from the state, government always finds money for what is considered important. 
 
Sheri Withers, Ward 1 – There was an attempted home invasion at her house by four white males 
who were juveniles, three wearing masks. They were apprehended nearby but it was an 
extremely nerve wrecking experience. Support services are needed to help parents support youth.  
 
Kim Bush, Ward 2 – Thank you to the Mayor for allowing her extra time to speak at the previous 
meeting. Vandalism is a significant part of the youth gun violence. Police engagement with the 
unhoused community is needed. The County has money to help homeless. 
 
Martin Chartrand, Ward 3 – The parking ban on the top side of Kennedy Park, by Walnut Street 
and Spruce Street, should be lifted because it is negatively impacting the food pantry and 
farmer’s market. 
 
Nathan Pearl – For 141 years, this country has had the ability to build skyscrapers; we need to 
solve the issues for the unhoused.  
 
Jessica Donavan, business owner – Expressed concerns about the certificate of occupancy 
process for residential development.  Her employer has recently built several new homes and 
just learned about the revised requirements for certificates of occupancy, and this is delaying the 
sale of the properties. 
 
Jim Hafford, Ward 3 – Use the AI cameras to track ongoing drug transactions, no need to 
reinvent the wheel, look at best practices from other cities around the country. 
 
CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT 
 
1) The Cart to Curb informational sessions are well received and continuing. 
2) The Community Ambassadors program has 36 volunteers 
3) The plans for the Balloon Festival are coming together 
4) The City recently hired two new police officers. 
5) Enhanced signage for Kennedy Park has been posted 
6) The Public Art Committee recently authorized two projects to help clean up graffiti in 
public spaces 
7) There will be a Meet and Greet in Ward 7 hosted with Councilor Martel 
 
AMENDMENT TO THE TRAFFIC SCHEDULE TO ADD ADDITIONAL 15-MINUTE 
PARKING SPOTS ON PINE STREET FROM HORTON STREET TO 
PRINCE STREET ALLEY 
 
VOTE (285-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine:
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 4, 2026 
                             
3 
 
 
To approve an amendment to the Traffic Schedule, Section 23, “Parking Time Regulated, 15 
minutes, 9 am to 9 pm”, to add additional 15-minute parking spaces on Pine Street from Horton 
Street to Prince Street Alley.   Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
AUTHORIZATION TO ACCEPT TRANSFER OF FORFEITURE FUNDS 
 
VOTE (286-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
That pursuant to Title 15, Maine Revised Statutes Annotated, Section 5824(3) and Section 
5822(4)(A), the City Council hereby acknowledges and approves the transfer of proceeds from the 
sale of a 9mm Taurus Pistol, S/N: 1GA91230 or any portion thereof, in t he case of the State of 
Maine vs. Carlton J. Enos, ANDCD -CR-2024-00749 Court Records, being funds forfeited 
pursuant to the court process. It is further acknowledged that these funds shall be credited to the 
‘City of Lewiston Drug Enforcement Program’ account.   Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, APPROVING THE DISPOSITION OF 35 BEECHWOOD AVENUE 
 
VOTE (287-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chttim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To approve the Order, Approving the Disposition of 35 Beechwood Avenue: 
 
Whereas, the City Council voted to sell the tax acquired parcel located at 35 Beechwood Avenue  
at their 2/25/2020 meeting and 
 
Whereas, the City received an offer for the parcel through the City’s Realtor DuBois Realty; and 
 
Whereas, Ashley Woodbury offered $1,000 for 35 Beechwood Avenue  
 
Now, T herefore, B e It Ordered by the C ity Council of the C ity of L ewiston, to approve the 
disposition of 35 Beechwood Avenue and authorize the City Administrator to execute all necessary 
legal documents. 
 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
APPOINTMENT TO THE LEWISTON HOUSING AUTHORITY BOARD OF 
COMMISSIONERS 
 
VOTE (288-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Nagine, seconded by Councilor Chittim: 
 
To confirm the Mayor’s nomination and to appoint the following resident as a member of the 
Board of Commissioners of the Lewiston Housing Authority:
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 4, 2026 
                             
4 
 
Craig Tribuno, 62 Sherbrooke Avenue, term to expire Sept. 17, 2029 – citizen representative 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FINAL PASSAGE REGARDING AMENDMENTS TO THE 
SOLID WASTE ORDINANCE TO DEFINE THE AUTOMATED SIDE LOAD TRASH 
COLLECTION PROGRAM 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing. 
 
VOTE (289-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
That the proposed amendments to the City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 62 “Solid Waste”, to 
define the automated side load trash collection program, receive final passage by a roll call vote. 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FIRST & FINAL PASSAGE FOR AN EXTENSION OF THE 
MORATORIUM ORDINANCE REGARDING RENT INCREASES FOR LOTS IN 
MOBILE HOME PARKS 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. Matt Roy, Ward 
6 – The proposed ordinance is very complex, keep it simple like so many other towns have done 
– Auburn, Old Orchard Beach, Brunswick, Kittery, Saco, Sanford.  Can’t keep kicking the can 
down the road on projects.  John Geary, resident of Fox Run mobile home park – Has seen the 
draft ordinance, it is the best in the state, park owners want protections until the ordinance is in 
place, support the moratorium. John Horton, co-owner of Sunset Gardens Mobile Home Park – 
This process started in the Governor’s Office, incorrect and misleading information is circulating 
around the state, we did not have a lot rent problem in Lewiston until this ordinance was 
proposed, this is business.  Chris Saroy, co -owner of Sunset Gardens Mobile Home Park – 
compliments to the Housing Committee, they are very dedicated volunteers who have invested a 
lot of time on this issue, they have done quality work and have good intentions, but this 
ordinance is ignoring realities.  Jeff Padham, Ward 3 and member of Housing Committee – the 
Committee never took a vote to ask for an extension of the moratorium, it is the Council’s job to 
protect the economy, put a 5% cap on lot rent increases to allow more time for the Committee to 
study the issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing. 
 
VOTE (290-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
That the proposed Moratorium Ordinance regarding Rent Increases for Lots in Mobile Home 
Parks, to be effective September 29, 2026, receive first passage by a roll call vote. 
Did Not Pass - Vote 2-5 (Mayor Sheline and Councilor Harriman in favor) 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND APPROVAL OF ORDER, AUTHORIZING THE CITY 
ADMINISTRATOR TO EXECUTE A CREDIT ENHANCEMENT AGREEMENT FOR 
THE SOLEIL MULTI-FAMILY HOUSING PROJECT
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 4, 2026 
                             
5 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. Ronnie Paradis, 
Ward 6 – Where is the school department going to educate all of the additional kids arriving in 
town as a result of this large development, there are 6,000 kids in the system now and it is at 
capacity. The Mayor then closed the hearing. 
 
VOTE (291-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To adopt the Order, Authorizing the City Administrator to Execute a Credit Enhancement 
Agreement for the Soleil Multi-Family Housing Project: 
Ordered, that the City Council hereby authorizes the City Administrator to execute a 
Development Assistance and Credit Enhancement Agreement, together with any related 
documents deemed necessary, between the City of Lewiston and Soleil Apartments LP, 
substantially in the form presented, to facilitate the development of a 72-unit affordable multi-
family housing project located at 61 Ash Street. 
Be It Further Ordered, that the Agreement shall establish an Affordable Housing Development 
District pursuant to Maine's Affordable Housing Tax Increment Financing (TIF) statute and 
provide for the reimbursement of seventy-three percent (73%) of the captured tax increment to 
Soleil Apartments LP over a twenty (20) year period, with the remaining twenty-seven percent 
(27%) retained by the City, subject to the terms and conditions of the Agreement and State 
approval. 
Be It Further Ordered, that all reimbursements shall be made only after the developer has paid 
one hundred percent (100%) of all annual property taxes due and only for eligible project costs 
as authorized under Maine law and the approved Development Program. 
Be It Further Ordered, that the City Administrator is authorized to execute any ancillary 
agreements, certifications, amendments, and documents necessary to implement the Agreement, 
provided such actions are consistent with the intent of this Order and approved as to form by the 
Corporation Counsel. 
 
Passed - Vote 6-1 (Councilor Martel opposed) 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND RESOLVE, AUTHORIZING A SUPPLEMENTAL 
APPROPRIATION IN THE AMOUNT OF $200,000 FROM THE SALARY RESERVE 
ACCOUNT TO COVER THE COS OF ADDITIONAL POLICE OVERTIME IN 
RESPONSE TO SHOOTINGS AND VIOLENT CRIME THAT HAVE BEEN 
OCCURRING WITHIN THE CITY OF LEWISTON 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. Melissa Dunn, 
Lewiston – Be aware of amendments regarding technology, should be a separate agenda item. 
Larry Gilbert, Lewiston – Supports the amendment, need tools to do job, the police department 
needs this new technology tool, critically important to give the proper tools for the job, larger 
cities have helicopters for same purpose.  Martin Chartrand, Ward 3 – This has been presented 
as a black and white issue -if vote against, don’t support public safety, this is not true. Having 
technology does not necessarily make things safer.  Matt Roy, Ward 6 – There was $877,000 in
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 4, 2026 
                             
6 
 
the overtime budget that was approved for the police department and now 35 days into the new 
fiscal year, they are asking for $200,000 more. Amran Osmand, Ward 3 – Want all children safe, 
youth family involvement has role to play, need to invest in youth in community infrastructure – 
basketball leagues, soccer leagues, mentors in the evening, activities for prevention efforts. 
Elizabeth Eames, Ward 3 – Read a letter on behalf of a resident, calling for more support for 
young people. Jen Hogan, CEO of Community Credit Union - Appreciate hearing the proposal 
tonight, this is Step 1. Julia Harper, Ward 4 – Relieved to see a plan in writing, more investment 
in youth is needed. The Mayor then closed the hearing. 
 
VOTE (292-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Longchamps: 
 
To amend the Resolve to appropriate an additional $55,000 from Fund Balance for the 
acquisition of a self-deploying drone.  Did Not Pass - Vote 2-5 (Councilors Longchamps and 
Martel in favor) 
 
VOTE (293-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Longchamps: 
 
To approve the Resolve, Authorizing a Supplemental Appropriation in the amount of $200,000 
from the Salary reserve account to cover the cost of additional police overtime in response to 
shootings and violent crime that have been occurring within the City of Lewiston: 
 
Whereas, The City of Lewiston has been experiencing shootings and violent crime; and 
Whereas, The need for public safety in the City of Lewiston is essential; and 
Whereas, The City of Lewiston is committed to being a place of pride, aspiration, diversity, 
engagement and accomplishment; and 
Whereas, The funding of additional police overtime will allow the police department to initiate a 
robust public safety plan. 
Now, Therefore, Be It Resolved by the City Council of the City of Lewiston to Authorize a 
Supplemental Appropriation in the amount of $200,000 from the Salary Reserve account to 
cover the cost of additional police overtime in response to shootings and violent crime that have 
been occurring within the City of Lewiston.   
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
At this time, the Mayor called for a ten-minute recess, and the meeting would reconvene at 
10:00pm. 
 
AMENDMENTS TO THE CITY’S ETHICS POLICY, POLICY MANUAL NUMBER 94 
 
VOTE (294-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Longchamps, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To postpone this item to the next City Council meeting.  Passed - Vote 7-0
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 4, 2026 
                             
7 
 
ORDER, DIRECTING THE CITY ADMINISTRATOR TO EXPLORE THE 
DISSOLUTION OF THE LEWISTON AUBURN RAILROAD COMPANY 
 
VOTE (295-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Nagine, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To postpone this item to the next City Council meeting.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, DIRECTING THE CITY ADMINISTRATOR TO REQUEST AN 
ADDITIONAL AGENCY LIQUOR STORE LICENSE FROM THE MAINE BUREAU 
OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES AND LOTTERY OPERATIONS 
 
The motion was continued to this Council meeting: 
 
VOTE (296-2026) 
 
To approve the Order, Directing the City Administrator to request an Additional Agency Liquor 
Store License from the Maine Bureau of Alcoholic Beverages and Lottery Operations. 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
No members of the public addressed the Council at this time. 
 
REPORTS AND UPDATES 
 
Councilor Chittim noted he is on the Lewiston Auburn Transit Committee and will be speaking 
with them about the possibility of going to the new senior center.  
 
OTHER BUSINESS 
 
Councilor Longchamps apologized for voting on Item 2 noting it impacts her business. Councilor 
Nagine asked to have a public hearing on the FERC licensing at the next meeting. Councilor Roy 
– Likes the idea of TIFs for new businesses and not housing, need more funding to help youth 
and have more mentoring, the Rec Dept should open up more grass fields for baseball and 
soccer, Public Works needs to do a traffic study at Sabattus and Rideout, there was a bad 
accident recently. Councilor Nagine said the Housing Committee should keep working on the 
mobile lot rent ordinance. 
 
EXECUTIVE SESSIONS 
VOTE (297-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Nagine, seconded by Councilor Chittim: 
 
To enter into an Executive Session pursuant to MRSA Title 1, section 405 (6) (D) to discuss Labor 
Negotiations regarding the Maine State Employees Association, Local 1989  and an Executive 
Session pursuant to MRSA Title 1, section 405(6)(A) to discuss a personnel matter. 
Passed - Vote 7-0
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 4, 2026 
                             
8 
 
Executive Session began at 10:20pm and ended at 11:00pm. 
 
VOTE (298-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Nagine, seconded by Councilor Harriman: 
 
To adjourn at 11:00 P.M.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
A true record, Attest: 
 
 
 
Kathleen M. Montejo, MMC  
City Clerk 
Lewiston, Maine
